newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Nov 22.

text.p: THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Reporting a A$2.1 billion net profit yesterday, up 6.8 per cent on last year's result, National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus said economic conditions would become increasingly difficult unless there was another interest rate cut. Argus predicted the Reserve Bank would cut another half a percentage point off official interest rates once it realised how soft the economy is in retail, manufacturing and construction. Page 1.

According to the Treasury's spring Economic Roundup, although there has been an uneven pattern of activity across sectors, there is little reason to alter the upbeat forecasts for solid economic growth and strong business investment during 1996/97 made inthe Budget. The Budget forecast economic growth at 3.5 percent in year-average terms. Page 3.

The Federal Court confirmed the power of the Australian Securities Commission yesterday, ruling that the wife of former Interwest hotel chain chief executive John Avram must attend an Australian Securities Commission hearing. Justice North said the
ASC's "mighty" powers were like those of the National Crime Authority and allowed it to question citizens "in relation to any matter that relates to a special investigation". Page 3.

A recent spate of selling in Fairfax Holdings Ltd shares has seen Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation quit its A$100 million stake and Fairfax's third largest shareholder, Bankers Trust Australia, increase its holding to just less than 13.5 percent. BT Autralia is allowed to lift its share to as high as 14.99 per cent, but its voting stake is limited to five per cent. Page 31.

Helix Resources managing director Rob Mosig remains unfazed by the stock market reaction to the Gawler Craton gold find, even though shares in his company have more than quadrupled in the past two weeks and Helix is now valued at almost A$100 million. The Gawler Craton gold rush has seen some small mining companies' share price more than double. Page 31.

A group of Australian and United States investors have combined to acquire an interest of up to 70 percent in the gas pipeline assets of Tenneco Energy Australia, including a majority interest in the 660 kilometre Moomba to Port Bonython petroleum liquid pipeline in South Australia and a similar stake in the just-completed Balera to Walumbilla gas pipeline stretching across Queensland. Page 31.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The National Australia Bank Ltd has posted the biggest annual profit ever for an Australian listed company with a record A$2.1 billion. Yesterday's figures showed a seven percent jump in profits and a 17 percent increase in total assets to A$173 billion. The news of the huge profit increased speculation that NAB was eyeing Westpac for a takeover. Page 23.

The News Corporation Ltd is believed to be shedding its stake in rival publisher John Fairfax , according to local brokers. Although news has not commented on the transactions, it is believed the group's five per cent stake,
worth about A$100 million, has been sold over the past few weeks. Page 23.

The Australian dollar crashed through the US80c barrier yesterday to reach a six-year high against the greenback. After heavy trading the dollar closed at US80.77c, which was more than US1c higher than on Wednesday and its highest level since October 1990. Page 23.

According to the 1996 Australian Financial Markets Report released yesterday, turnover on local financial markets declined last year. Turnover dropped from a peak of A$28 trillion in 1994/95 to A$27 trillion for 1995/96, prompting fears that Australia is losing ground as a regional financial centre. Page 23.

The power of institutional investors received a boost yesterday when the Australian Securities Commission put forward an issues paper on collective voting at company meetings. The ASC believes the present arrangement on collective voting is a
strong disincentive for institutional investors to participate fully in company meetings and is currently seeking comment on how the participation can be encouraged. Page 24.

Following a tour of MIM Holdings Ltd's Mt Isa and Ernest Henry operations this week, brokers and fund managers pushed MIM's share price up another four cents yesterday to A$1.78. However, Wilson HTM senior director of resources, Phil Hutchings, says a major shift in market sentiment on MIM is not under way and he has been advising clients to avoid MIM and copper stocks generally. Page 24.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The National Australia Bank yesterday posted the first A$2 billion-plus annual profit for a public company. Net profit for the bank increased 6.8 percent to A$2.1 billion for the year to September, with managing director Don Argus promising the bank's peformance "would continue to improve". Page 27.

News Corporation is believed to have disposed of its four per cent share holding in John Fairfax Holdings, indicating the media group is not confident the Federal Government will change laws regarding foreign ownership. News is believed to have sold the 10.3 million shares last month at an estimated profit of A$6 million. Page 27.

The Federal Treasury has defended its Budget forecasts of strong economic growth this financial year despite increasing evidence of a slowdown. In its latest quarterly economic review, Treasury maintains 3.5 per cent economic growth and a 14 per
cent rise in business investment will be met. Page 27.

Entertainment group, Amalgamated Holdings has posted a small drop in first quarter operating profit from A$19.6 million to A$19 million. Chairman Alan Rydge believes slow trading in cinema chain Greater Union and fewer skiers at the Thredbo resort are behind the slow-down in activity. Page 29.

Depending on shareholder approval being given at a special meeting on December 20, Australian insurer MMI is about to enter a deal which would give it a 20 per cent stake in Singapore's Allianz Insurance for A$23.9 million and in return secure 20 per cent of MMI for Allianz, lifting its stake to around 38 per cent. Page 29.

Hoyts Cinemas will sell 22.2 million new shares at A$2.75 each in an effort to raise A$66.1 million. The funds will be used partly for cinema deals under negotiation in the US and western Europe and the rest will go towards acquiring a
controlling 35 per ent of Mexico City-based multiplex group Cinemex. Page 29.
THE AGE

In a result National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus described as consistent and workmanlike, NAB became the first listed Australian company to crack the A$2 billion profit barrier yesterday, reporting a 6.8 percent increase in its bottom-line result to A$2.1 billion. Page C1.

National Australia Bank managing director Don Argus yesterday forecast another cut in official interest rates within the next couple of months, claiming Australia's three key industries, manufacturing, building and construction and retail, were "really flat". The prediction came as official company profit figures were released, showing quarterly profits overall rose only 0.2 per cent to A$5.24 billion, seasonally adjusted. Page C1.

In a move that signals Rupert Murdoch holds little hope of the Federal Government changing limits on foreign media ownership, News Corporation is believed to have quit its four per cent shareholding in John Fairfax Holdings. With Fairfax shares trading btween A$2.66 and A$2.80 during October, News would have made a profit of no more than A$6 million. Page C1.

Pharmaceutical company CSL posted net earnings of A$29 million in 1995-96, an 18 per cent rise on the previous year. Managing director Dr Brian McNamee said after yesterday's annual meeting that CSL is on track to better that performance despite the Government's decision to cut research and development assistance. Page C2.

The Federal Government unveiled a new research and development program yesterday which will see it receive royalties from the commercialisation of some high-tech projects. An addition to the guidelines for the Start program, of A$520
million in funding oer four years, all but A$40 million relies on the Senate passing legislation which scraps syndication and reduces tax breaks in other schemes. Page C3.

Raising A$61.1 million in an institutional placement, Hoyts Cinemas has agreed to make a capital injection of about A$28 million into Mexico's pre-eminent cinema operator, Cinemex, over the next 12 months, becoming the major shareholder with 35 per cent. Hoyts is also working on a further three or four acquisition opportunities in western Europe and North America. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
